overall: The AG found that the Chair individually violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a quorum of the Board his opinion on a Board-jurisdiction matter, ordered the email disclosed, declined the agenda/staff allegation, and cautioned the Board on its slow complaint response.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated by email after the Chair emailed a quorum of members about the Charter Review Committee continuing past its deadline.
allegations.key_passage: we find that Chair Magnani individually violated the Open Meeting Law by sending an email sharing his opinion on a matter within the Board's jurisdiction to a quorum of the Board.

allegations.summary: General allegation that the Board communicates privately and/or uses staff to set meeting agendas.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because, even if true, it would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Board took about four months to respond to the complaint, beyond the 14-business-day response requirement.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the Board took four months to respond to this complaint.

remedy: Disclose Chair Magnani's email to the public within 30 days of receipt of this determination, if it has not done so already.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to disclose Chair Magnani's email to the public within 30 days of receipt of this determination, if it has not done so already.
